previous_action: Gaius Maximus Valerius begins the next major part of his expedition by leaving the ravine fortress under a reliable garrison and taking the main body deeper into the territory used by the regional band. He advances through several routes at once, using scouts trained in July to compare roads, water sources, settlements and concealed approaches before committing the column. He intends to find and break the band's wider network rather than chase isolated parties, while keeping the fortress and estate road behind him as a secure line of supply.

continuity.campaign_development: In August 60 BCE, Valerius began the next major phase of his expedition by leaving the ravine fortress under garrison and taking the main body deeper into territory used by the regional band. Multiple routes were surveyed before the column committed to the interior. Reports and field evidence revealed a distributed network of hidden stores and a supply road connecting it to cultivated holdings. Valerius established a forward camp and began operating against the network supporting the band rather than simply pursuing isolated parties.
